findings.change: Adopted LANE_RULES' one-PR rule and wrote its process conditions into the docstring ('Own commits'): the report is the branch's last own commit, written once (no draft report); a commit after the report is outside the rule and the process makes none. Lookups use --full-history (n2). Shown on toy repositories (toy_demo below).

Same rule: prereg, fold, build, outcomes and report are commits of one branch whose first-parent line runs from C_K; the lead enters only by merge commits whose first parent is the branch, so no lead commit, merged or pushed directly, lies on that line; the branch reaches the lead as the second parent of a merge. Toy A shows a direct lead commit (spec/, laws/) and a merged PR before the branch's lead merge, and later lead commits after the merge (one editing the report), none counted.

tests_m3/_i69.py::timeline now trusts none of holon's derived fields: logs inside [from_block, fetch_block], of the proxy and unique; proxy addresses equal the sidecar's, the messenger's the queue's last in-window implementation's MESSENGER word (sidecar acquisition.proxies.messenger.immutable); upgrades rebuilt from raw Upgraded logs, each confirmed by its committed receipt (transactionHash, blockNumber, status 0x1, the same log at its index) and decoded from it, its implementation matched on its committed code; the EIP-1967 implementation slot read at the fetch block must name the last Upgraded log's implementation (the scan's completeness at its end; A3 now scans to the fetch block, upgrades after the window listed apart); the whitelist address is the low 20 bytes of the queue's word at its whitelistChecker slot from solc's layout (sidecar acquisition.whitelist.slot_of). A3's snapshot format gains window, implementation_slot and the whitelist's proxy, slot and block. Probed on a fabricated snapshot with matching stubbed: the plumbing and seven refusals (slot, queue address, messenger address, whitelist slot, receipt log, log outside the window, fetch block).
